facts.statement: Telmatornis lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Maastrichtian age.
Fossils of Telmatornis were found in the Navesink Formation of New Jersey, dating to the early Maastrichtian approximately 71 to 68 million years ago.
facts.quote: its remains were found in the early Maastrichtian (c.71-68 million years ago) Navesink Formation of New Jersey

facts.statement: Telmatornis is classified as a valid genus of prehistoric birds within the order Charadriiformes.
facts.quote: Telmatornis is a valid prehistoric bird genus which has been placed in Charadriiformes

facts.statement: There is ongoing uncertainty regarding the precise taxonomic placement of Telmatornis.
facts.quote: There is some uncertainty about its taxonomic affiliation

facts.statement: It is debated whether Telmatornis was evolutionarily related to grebes or if its wing structure was merely a case of convergent evolution.
facts.quote: It is thus unknown whether this apparent similarity to grebes represents an evolutionary relationship, or whether Telmatornis simply had a wing convergent on that of grebes and moved it like they do

facts.statement: A 2002 analysis of the forelimb skeleton found Telmatornis to be highly similar to the great crested grebe.
facts.quote: A cladistic analysis of the forelimb skeleton (Varricchio 2002) found it highly similar to the great crested grebe

facts.statement: Telmatornis possessed a humerus dorsal condyle that was not angled 20 to 30 degrees away from the long axis of the bone.
facts.quote: namely in that its dorsal condyle of the humerus was not angled at 20°–30° away from long axis of the humerus

facts.statement: The parent group for the genus Telmatornis is Charadriiformes.
The type species of the genus Telmatornis is Telmatornis priscus.
The time range for Telmatornis spans from the Maastrichtian to the Danian, between 72.2 and 61.66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Danian (72.2 to 61.66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The genus Telmatornis was described by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1870.
